title: session-reassembler-and-fine-grained-latency-contributors-dashboard
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: debugging SLO regressions often requires stitching together fragments from frontend request IDs, gateway hops, router handoffs, and backend runtime spans. Current dashboards surface aggregate per-route latency and token cost but lack an easy way to answer: which execution stage contributed most to tail latency for a given session or user flow? This PR introduces a session reassembler that groups spans and logs into session-level traces, computes a latency contribution matrix per-stage, and surfaces the results in a new dashboard with drilldowns. Design: 1) Session reassembler: deterministic session keys are computed from request headers (x-session-id when present), fallback to hashed {client_ip,user_agent,first-7-chars-of-request_id} for best-effort reconstruction. The reassembler runs as a bounded streaming transformer in the tracing pipeline and emits enriched spans tagged with session_id and stage_ordinal. 2) Late-arrival span stitching: implement a 30s buffer window with eventual reconciliation to handle spans that arrive after initial aggregation. Reconciled sessions are exported as session_digests which include per-stage p50/p90/p99 latencies and token counts. 3) Latency contribution matrix: for each session_digest we compute a normalized contribution vector across stages (gateway, auth, preproc, router, runtime-queue, runtime-exec, postproc). Matrices are aggregated into reservoir sketches to keep cardinality bounded. 4) Dashboard and alerting: new dashboard panel "Session Latency Matrix" visualizes dominant contributors for recent sessions and supports filtering by customer, route, and model. Introduce an SLO smoothing policy that uses session-level p95 of contribution instead of raw endpoint p95 to reduce noisy alerts from noisy frontends. 5) Backwards compatibility and opt-in: the reassembler is behind a rollout flag in the observability config; default is disabled. Customers can opt-in per-tenant. Rollout plan: enable in staging for 48 hours, shadow in prod for 7 days, then enable for 10% of traffic with metric gates. Telemetry: we emit reassembler.metrics.{sessions_processed,stitch_reconciliations,session_digest_size} and tagging on traces with session.id and stage.rank. Rollout notes: this PR adds additional memory for the buffering stage; sizing guidance documented in observability/README. Security: session keys do not materialize raw client_ip in exported payloads unless tenant-level PII flag is set; by default keys are salted and one-way hashed. Related work: this complements ENG-1942 (sampling improvements) and OBS-73 (session-based alerting).
commit_summary: feat(observability): add session reassembler transformer and session_digest export; feat(tracing): late-arrival stitcher and reconciliation; perf(tracing): reservoir sketch for contribution matrices; ui(dashboards): session latency matrix and drilldowns; docs: rollout and sizing guidance; test: unit+integration for reassembler and reconciliation
review_conversation: Aidan Keller: Can you clarify the semantics of the fallback session key? Maya Chen: Fallback uses a salted hash of client_ip+user_agent+req_prefix; salted per-tenant and not reversible. Priya Nair: The 30s buffer seems small for some tenants with eventual log shipping; any plan? Maya Chen: We reconciled to make the window configurable and added a reconnect/reconciliation metric; default remains 30s to bound memory. Diego Ruiz: Reservoir sketches look good but please add a test for cardinality drift. Maya Chen: Added tests to integration suite and a benchmark in scripts/size_estimator. Priya Nair: Approve after CI pass. Aidan Keller: Left a small nit on the UI (color scale) — updated in follow-up commit. Diego Ruiz: Verified metrics emission and endorses merge.
ci_checks: CI: unit (pass), integration (pass), lint (pass), ui-typecheck (pass), e2e-observability (flaky->rerun->pass). Observability pipeline job initially failed on protobuf lint, fixed in commit 3. Full CI green on second run.
release_notes: Adds an opt-in session reassembler for reconstructing traces across hops, per-session latency contribution matrices, a new Session Latency Matrix dashboard with drilldowns, SLO smoothing policy using session-level contributions, and observability metrics for rollout and sizing. No breaking changes by default; opt-in per-tenant.
notes: Sizing guidance added under docs/observability/README.md; may require observability team to coordinate with infra for buffer memory when enabling for high-cardinality tenants.
